question.title: Amendment No 1: Partisan Election Of Members Of District School Boards

source.name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections, Initiatives / Amendments / Revisions Database, detail page "PARTISAN ELECTION OF MEMBERS OF DISTRICT SCHOOL BOARDS"

ballot_text.source_title: Ballot Number 1, Election Year 2024: PARTISAN ELECTION OF MEMBERS OF DISTRICT SCHOOL BOARDS
ballot_text.type_quote: Proposing amendments to the State Constitution

fact.quote: Proposing amendments to the State Constitution to require members of a district school board to be elected in a partisan election rather than a nonpartisan election
fact.why: HJR 31 changes how school board members are elected; the only tax words in the text are existing language on school boards setting school district tax rates, which it does not change. No tax or fee is imposed. Inferred.

source.name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections, Initiatives / Amendments / Revisions Database, detail page "PARTISAN ELECTION OF MEMBERS OF DISTRICT SCHOOL BOARDS"

question.title: Amendment No 3: Adult Personal Use Of Marijuana

source.name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections, full text of the measure (PDF linked "View Full Text" on the detail page); read in full, searched for tax, fee, levy, assess, licen*, revenue, charge, fine, penalt*

ballot_text.source_title: Ballot Number 3, Election Year 2024: Adult Personal Use of Marijuana

fact.quote: If legal today, sales of non-medical marijuana would be subject to sales tax and would remain so if voters approve this amendment.
fact.why: The initiative text (Art. X, s. 29, read in full) allows adult personal use and licensed sales and lets the Legislature license other entities; it imposes and sets no tax or fee. The Financial Impact Estimating Conference (linked from the DOS page) says sales tax applies under existing law and "would remain so", and that regulatory costs "will probably be offset by regulatory fees" under "A new regulatory structure" whose design "cannot be fully known until the legislature acts", so any fee would come from later law, not this amendment. Closest call of the group; inferred.

source.name: Florida Financial Impact Estimating Conference, statement linked from the Division of Elections' detail page

question.title: Amendment No 4: Amendment To Limit Government Interference With Abortion

source.name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections, full text of the measure (PDF linked "View Full Text" on the detail page); read in full, searched for tax, fee, levy, assess, licen*, revenue, charge, fine, penalt*

ballot_text.source_title: Ballot Number 4, Election Year 2024: Amendment to Limit Government Interference with Abortion

fact.quote: Except as provided in Article X, Section 22, no law shall prohibit, penalize, delay, or restrict abortion before viability or when necessary to protect the patient’s health, as determined by the patient’s healthcare provider.
fact.why: The entire operative text (quoted) is one sentence limiting laws on abortion; it has no tax or fee wording. The Financial Impact Estimating Conference statement (fiec_2024_a4.txt) speaks of effects on state costs and revenues, not of any tax or fee imposed. Inferred.

question.title: Amendment No 5: Annual Adjustments To The Value Of Certain Homestead Exemptions

source.name: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections, Initiatives / Amendments / Revisions Database, detail page "ANNUAL ADJUSTMENTS TO THE VALUE OF CERTAIN HOMESTEAD EXEMPTIONS"

ballot_text.source_title: Ballot Number 5, Election Year 2024: ANNUAL ADJUSTMENTS TO THE VALUE OF CERTAIN HOMESTEAD EXEMPTIONS
ballot_text.type_quote: Proposing an amendment to the State Constitution to require an annual adjustment for inflation

fact.quote: to require an annual adjustment for inflation to the value of current or future homestead exemptions that apply solely to levies other than school district levies
fact.why: CS/HJR 7017 raises homestead exemption values with inflation, which reduces tax over time. The full text was read and contains no provision that imposes, authorizes or sets any tax or fee. Inferred.
